summary: rollup-plugin-polyfill-helper fetches and eval()s remote payload from rest-icon-helper.store
details: The package presents itself as a rollup polyfill / SVG-icon helper, but its exported functions getPlugin/setPlugin/getPluginExten construct a URL from split string constants (protocol + separator + subdomain 'rest-icon-helper' + domain 'store' + path '/icons/'), issue an HTTP request to that host with a decoy 'bearrtoken: logo' header, and pass the response body to eval(JSON.parse(b)). Any consumer invocation of these functions causes attacker-controlled JavaScript delivered from rest-icon-helper.store to execute in the caller's Node.js process, granting arbitrary code execution on the installer's build/runtime machine. The split-string URL construction, mimic naming, and iconDomain misdirection map are consistent with deliberate evasion rather than a legitimate CDN helper.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
